title: Many rolls
statement:
As the number of rolls $n$ grows, what happens to $1 - (5/6)^n$, the chance of at least one six?

[_]{a}

choices: It gets closer and closer to 1
explanations: 5/6 is the chance of no six in **one** roll.
1/6 is the chance of a six on one roll; more rolls give more chances.
That is what happens to $(5/6)^n$, the chance of **no** six.

hints: What happens to $(5/6)^n$ when n is large?
A number below 1 raised to a big power gets tiny.
1 minus a tiny number is close to 1.
solution: $(5/6)^n \to 0$, so $1 - (5/6)^n \to 1$: with enough rolls a six is almost certain.
